title: A Bounded Planetary Stability Vector Space and Monte Carlo Prioritization Framework Applied to the NASA Exoplanet Archive: Identification of LHS 1140 b as a Structurally Robust Temperate Candidate
content: A bounded planetary stability framework is constructed from the NASA Exoplanet Archive by defining a class-normalized state vector \( (R,H,M,S) \) of catalog proxies and a windowed scalar projection, \( \Phi_p \). Planetary ripeness is defined as a time-weighted residence functional within this bounded window, separating instantaneous placement from accumulated residence time. A five-tier pipeline enforces observability discipline and reproducibility. Tier~1 constructs the archive-scale space using robust normalization within radius classes. Tier~2 applies thermodynamic and temporal gates on insolation, equilibrium temperature, orbital eccentricity, and stellar age. Tier~3 derives bulk diagnostics (density, surface gravity, escape velocity and, in this version, an implied core mass fraction) without imputation. Tier~4 adds follow-up feasibility proxies. Tier~5 propagates measurement uncertainties through Monte Carlo sampling (\( N_{\rm MC}=2\times10^4 \)), merging uncertainty fields from the Planetary Systems table, resolving duplicate catalog entries with a deterministic completeness-aware rule, and applying conservative floors only where published errors are absent. Under the strict configuration, which uses a radius-defined small-planet class (\( R_p\le1.8\,\Rearth \)), the cascade reduces \( 39{,}386 \) archive rows to a single surviving candidate, LHS~1140~b. For this planet the pipeline derives a bulk density of \( 5.95\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}} \), an escape velocity of \( 1.80\,v_{\rm esc,\oplus} \), and a Tier~5 median Ripeness score of \( 0.947 \) (a relative score, not a fraction) with unit pass probability across all gates. The implied core mass fraction, \( -0.08\pm0.09 \), lies below the range of known rocky planets, in agreement with recent mass, radius, and JWST transmission results that identify LHS~1140~b as a water world or a planet with a thin envelope rather than a rocky super-Earth. The framework therefore isolates a well-characterised, temperate, high-gravity planet around an old host star; it does not establish a rocky composition, and its single survivor partly reflects how few small temperate planets have complete catalog data.
